sample_unit: ChatGPT responses to FAQs about geriatric syndromes

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT responses (Flesch-Kincaid Reading Ease and Grade Level)
links.effect: Mean FKRE score 25.2 and mean FKGL score 14.5; text very difficult to read, best understood by college graduates.
links.quote: The mean FKRE score of the texts was 25.2, while the mean FKGL score was 14.5.

links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT-generated patient information versus appropriate level
links.effect: Mean FKGL 14.5 and FKRE 25.2; text very difficult to read and best understood by college graduates.
links.quote: Moreover, the text generated by ChatGPT was very difficult to read and best understood by college graduates.

links.outcome: Geriatrician-rated accuracy of ChatGPT answers against current guidelines (0-4 scale)
links.effect: Overall mean accuracy 88% (3.52/4); lowest for sarcopenia diagnosis (2.0) and depression treatment (2.5).
links.quote: Responses generated for sarcopenia diagnosis and depression treatment in older adults had the lowest accuracy scores (2.0 and 2.5, respectively).

screen.reason: Evaluates the accuracy and readability of ChatGPT on frequently asked questions about geriatric syndromes using clinician grading and readability formulas, but does not test a specific deployment safeguard or practice intervention.
